findings.description: The inline user policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's static access key yields full control over compute, storage and serverless, including privilege-escalation paths such as ec2:RunInstances or lambda:CreateFunction with an existing instance profile / execution role.

A permanent IAM access key is provisioned for a human-style IAM user rather than using role-based, short-lived credentials, and no pgp_key is supplied, so the secret and ses_smtp_password are stored in cleartext in Terraform state. Combined with the wildcard policy attached to the same user, a state file leak equals full account-level compromise of EC2, S3 and Lambda.

The IAM user carries a wildcard inline policy but no permissions_boundary and no MFA-conditioned access, so there is no secondary control limiting the blast radius of a stolen programmatic credential.

The `secret` output exposes aws_iam_access_key.user.encrypted_secret. Since no pgp_key was set this attribute is empty, but the output is not marked sensitive, so any credential-bearing value it resolves to would be printed to the console and recorded in plan/apply logs and state; the paired `username` output further identifies the privileged principal.
